work.title: Reusable recovery-methods engine
authority: Direct user request: minimal reusable recovery methods engine

intent.productGoal: Preserve a governed distinction between observed evidence and modeled remaining recovery without altering existing QoR analytics.
intent.capability: Provide an independently callable contract for collection-distribution, percent-of-charges, and composite recovery methods, including evidence state, an as-of/reconstruction boundary, and segment-level overrides.
architecturalIntent: Keep the new recovery engine separate from the existing analytics path until an explicit integration decision is made.
Represent money as integer cents and preserve method/evidence provenance in results.
invariants: The engine must not modify source evidence or manufacture observed collections.
Items outside the as-of boundary must not contribute to recovery output.
Each eligible item is assigned at most one composite segment.
acceptanceEvidence: Focused node tests cover all three methods, evidence states, as-of exclusion, reconstruction boundaries, and segment override precedence.
Core typecheck and existing core tests demonstrate the analytics path remains unchanged.

decisions.decision: Expose a standalone recovery contract rather than changing analyze() or legacy MethodProfile behavior.
decisions.rationale: The direct request forbids changing existing analytics behavior, while the standalone API is reusable and permits later governed integration.

observedBehaviour: The standalone engine returns modeled recovery only, retains input evidence references, and emits exclusions for as-of mismatch, missing charge basis, and insufficient method evidence.
Focused tests demonstrated collection-distribution reconstruction filtering, exact percent-of-charges cent rounding, first-match composite overrides, and boundary enforcement.
Core typecheck passed without modifying packages/core/src/analytics.ts.

evidence.result: Standalone reusable recovery engine; no analytics integration or legacy analytics edit.

divergences.observed: An unrelated concurrently untracked fixture test, RR-COHORT-CURVE-001, expected observed cash of 80000 cents but received 60000 cents.

durableKnowledge: Recovery-method policy is a modeled, approval-bound concern and is intentionally not wired into legacy analytics by this work.
